subject: Performance SLO / Private VPC qualification - post-call recap
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Danielle Park <dpark@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Performance SLO / Private VPC qualification - post-call recap

Hi Danielle — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and next steps so we’re aligned on the performance/latency picture for ACME’s private VPC deployment: 

Summary of customer targets (as discussed):
- End-to-end inference latency SLO: p95 <= 200ms for 64-token responses (streaming enabled).
- Concurrency / throughput: support 50 concurrent streaming sessions (approx 20 QPS sustained with bursts to 60).
- Streaming behavior: chunked server-sent events with first-token delivery <100ms when cold-cache is not in play.
- Internal latency budget: team expects <50ms network RTT from ACME app hosts to Redwood private endpoints in us-west-2.

Key network items we need from ACME to validate sizing and run the lab:
1) Network path and topology details (Transit Gateway/Peering/VPN) + egress path if traffic will leave ACME VPC.
2) Current VPN config (IKE/IPSec) and any throughput caps configured on the VPN gateway.
3) A few packet captures or traceroutes from the app host to the proposed endpoint (us-west-2).
4) Expected concurrency profile (ramp schedule) and any streaming window/timeouts on your side.

What Redwood will do next:
- SE team (cc’d) will run a short connectivity and throughput checklist: iperf3, traceroute, and a small prompt latency test using a private lab endpoint.
- We’ll validate TLS termination options (mutual TLS or SRV private endpoint) and provide recommended port/opening list.
- If the network path shows >80ms RTT we’ll propose an edge routing/peering option or suggestion to move a small subset of inference traffic to a closer region.

Next steps / ask from you:
- Share the network path/traceroute and VPN config files mentioned above. Attachments are fine.
- Confirm a 2-hour window next week where your networking/SRE folks can join a lab session (we recommend Tuesday or Wednesday morning PST).
- Point us to the person on your team who will handle firewall/VPN changes.

I’ve attached a short checklist of tests the SE team will run. If any of the targets above are off, we’ll call them out clearly in the lab.

Thanks — I’ll coordinate with Marissa and Marcus on SE availability once we get your windows.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: performance-checklist.pdf (stub)

From: Danielle Park <dpark@acme-corp.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: SRE Team <sre@acme-corp.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 09:14:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLO / Private VPC qualification - post-call recap

Hi Jordan — thanks for the concise recap. Confirming the targets are correct from ACME’s side. A few details and files attached:

- Our infra is in AWS us-west-2, fronted by a Transit Gateway. Most app hosts are in a private subnet behind TGW.
- VPN: we currently have an IPSec tunnel from our on-premcolo to a VGW; throughput historically limited to ~600 Mbps due to older edge devices.
- RTT: internal tests to our public internet exit show ~18–28ms to us-west-2 endpoints; we’ll run traceroutes to the IP you provide.

Attachments: network-trace.pdf (trace + small pcap), vpn-config.txt (current IPSec/IKE profile).

Couple of questions:
1) Does Redwood support mutual TLS for private endpoints (we prefer mTLS for service-to-service auth)?
2) For streaming, do you recommend persistent TCP (websocket) or SSE? We prefer websocket but can adapt.

We can do a lab on Wednesday 24 Feb 09:00–11:00 PST; SRE will join. Our network owner is James Li (jli@acme-corp.com).

Thanks,
Danielle
Director, Platform Engineering | ACME Corp
dpark@acme-corp.com

---
Attachments: network-trace.pdf (stub), vpn-config.txt (stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 09:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLO / Private VPC qualification - post-call recap

Sooj, Marcus — looping you in to run the lab with ACME next Wednesday 24 Feb 09:00–11:00 PST (confirmed by Danielle).

Goal: validate the network path and confirm we can meet p95 <= 200ms for the 64-token streaming flows at target concurrency (50 concurrent sessions). Primary tests:
- iperf3 (1 min runs) from ACME app host to our private lab endpoint to measure TCP throughput and packet loss.
- Traceroute and pings to validate hop-level RTT and MTU path.
- Small prompt latency test: 100 short prompts (64 tokens) distributed across simulated concurrency to measure first-byte and chunked-latency.

Notes / runbook links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cRunbookLab (lab checklist) and HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567 (ACME).

If the IPSec device caps throughput ~600Mbps that may be fine for our initial concurrency, but we want to identify whether bursts cause queueing that increases tail latency. If we see RTT >80ms we’ll propose a peering/exchange option or ask ACME to open a private endpoint in another AZ/region.

Can you confirm the exact endpoint IP we’ll use and whether we should enable mTLS for the lab (Danielle asked about mTLS).

Thanks — I’ll be on the call to coordinate product-side questions.

-Marissa
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Danielle Park <dpark@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, James Li <jli@acme-corp.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 10:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLO / Private VPC qualification - post-call recap

Thanks Danielle — Wednesday 24 Feb 09:00–11:00 PST is locked. We’ll use the private lab endpoint IP: 10.88.55.23 (placeholder until we provision a dedicated endpoint in your VPC). 

Answers to your questions quickly:
- mTLS: yes, we support mutual TLS for private endpoints and can enable cert-based auth for the lab. SE will walk through cert chain and rotation.
- Streaming: Websockets are fully supported and typically give slightly lower head-of-line latency for chunked responses; SSE is also supported if you prefer HTTP-based delivery. For the lab we’ll test both (primary = websocket).

Deliverables for the lab:
1) We’ll run the iperf3 + traceroute suite.
2) We’ll run 3 x 1-minute concurrency ramps (10 -> 25 -> 50 streams) measuring p50/p95/p99 for first-token and per-chunk latency.
3) SE will provide a short report within 24 hours with recommendations (peer, endpoint placement, VPN config changes).

James — can you share any maintenance windows that would block the 24th? Also please send over a read-only IAM or a temp jump host access if you want us to initiate tests from inside your VPC.

Jordan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai
